title: Finite Verdier coefficient diagrams without numerical estimates
statement: Fix the finite-field datum D, a prime l distinct from its characteristic, a finite extension E of Q_l and a separated finite-type scheme X over its algebraic closure [def-weil-finite-field-fiber, def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-proper-morphism]. At every positive coefficient level n+1 use the ordinary-etale dualizing term omega_n and its counit-defined coefficient transition u [lem-coef-finite-dualizing]; on the pro-etale site transport them by comparison pullback. On each site there exist normalized scalar tensor comparison isomorphisms and the prescribed normalized duality pairings [lem-weil-duality-pairing]. There is an ambient natural transformation S Hom(-,omega_n) -> Hom(S(-),omega_m), invertible on finite-Tor constructible inputs, and scalar extension preserves this domain [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. These transformations obey the evaluation equation, the double-dual square, identity quotient and quotient cocycle exactly as in cor-coef-finite-verdier. No numerical Tor estimate is asserted: in FiniteVerdierTwoSitesComparison both interval predicates are constant True.

proof.text: The regular coefficient sheaf is finite-Tor constructible of interval [0,0]. Its dual is omega by tensor-Hom adjunction, so Verdier preservation proves omega finite-Tor constructible. It also puts DK in the same domain for every allowed K. The flat-model theorem preserves this domain after reduction.

proof.text: On each finite range of levels form the target family omega with counit-defined invertible transitions u. Their normalized identity and cocycle give a FiniteTargetChangeFamily. Target-change coherence gives the comparison Hom(1,u) after the reduced-evaluation transpose, its isomorphism, evaluation, unit and cocycle. The canonical formula does not depend on the chosen finite range, so these identities hold at all natural-number levels; the ambient natural transformation comes from naturality of the transpose at arbitrary inputs.

proof.text: The domain-calculus tensor normalization is the normalization required by finiteVerdierOrdinaryExtension and its scalar representative: both are the actual localized ordinary scalar adjunction unit. Uniqueness of the tensor-Hom transpose identifies the normalized closed-record evaluations with the published pairing. Apply the bidual transpose theorem to the evaluation equations at K and DK to obtain the required double-dual square.

proof.text: Represent every pro-etale finite-Tor input by an etale input. Site target transport gives the scalar/site target square, evaluation and signed biduality compatibility and the normalized target cocycle. Transport along the fixed-module intrinsic realization equivalence; uniqueness of normalized tensor comparison and of adjoint transpose identifies the data with published pro-etale tensor and Hom. The target arrow is precisely pbcComparisonReduction.hom followed by comparison pullback of u. The constant-True interval clauses add no estimate. Identity quotients include exponent one.

theorem finiteVerdier_coefficient_diagrams
    (D : FiniteFieldDatum.{u}) (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (hl : l ≠ D.p)
    (E : Type u) [Field E] [Algebra (Padic l) E]
    [FiniteDimensional (Padic l) E] (X : Scheme.{u})
    [X.Over (Spec (.of D.k))]
    [IsSeparated (X ↘ Spec (.of D.k))]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType (X ↘ Spec (.of D.k))]
    [QuasiCompact (X ↘ Spec (.of D.k))] :
  @FiniteVerdierTwoSitesComparison X (finiteDualizingCoeff l E)
    (fun _n ↦ inferInstance) (fun {_ _} h ↦ finiteDualizingQuotient l E h)
    (finiteDualizingQuotient_id l E) (fun {_ _ _} h g ↦ finiteDualizingQuotient_comp l E h g)
    (finiteDualizingEtaleTerm l E D X)
    (fun n ↦ finiteTorConstructibleEtale l E (n + 1) (Nat.succ_le_succ (Nat.zero_le n)) X)
    (fun n ↦ finiteTorConstructibleProEtaleModule l E (n + 1)
      (Nat.succ_le_succ (Nat.zero_le n)) X)
    (fun _ _ _ _ ↦ True)
    (fun _ _ _ _ ↦ True)
    (fun {_ _} h ↦ finiteDualizingEtaleComparison l E D X h) 0
